descriptionHtml:
Case priority: P1 · our extension of a stated behaviour · ours: credentials in provider error text; nearest UAT OAT-05 step 1.

Suggestion A6 · hardening · not counted as a bug (was S2): our own stricter reading of OAT-05 step 1 (keys only): it shows no physician a wrong result, loses no data and shows no other physician's patient, so it is a suggestion, not a bug (Quinn 2026-10-14)

A vision failure forwards the provider's raw error (GCP project path, a masked key) to the browser: map provider errors to a category and status code first

Tickets: TFA-94423 ready for qa; TFA-94745 ready for qa · counts as a QA bug: no · found on: local (code review)

Note: Review 2026-10-14 (TFA-94423): vertex.ts:135/168 and phi.ts:191-196 are as found, but what reaches the browser is a project path and a masked key, not a usable key; OAT-05 step 1 is about keys, so this stricter reading is ours.

Approach · OAT-05 Keeping Data Secure / Real-PHI Readiness Gate · S30 A provider failure never carries a credential or a service-account identity to the client

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U1a No long-lived provider API key or credential (AWS, OpenAI, Google Vertex service account, Deepgram, SES) is present anywhere in client code: the web bundle and its served source maps, the iOS and And … (UAT OAT-05 step 1; TFA-94700 AC 5; TFA-94700 description ('No API keys client-side … UAT OAT-05 step 1'); TFA-94423 AC 1)

Test design technique: Error guessing (error-guessing) — Go straight for the places most likely to break (failures, double clicks, two tabs, a wrong clock, injected instructions).

Given The UAT commit's error paths: convex/ai/providers/vertex.ts toVertexConvexError (detail = first line of err.message, up to 300 characters), convex/ai/providers/bedrockErrors.ts toBedrockConvexError (class, name and status only), convex/lib/ses.ts (SES delivery errors), and the OpenAI path covered by S12's 'provider fa …

When Code-review each mapper and trace its ConvexError data to the client (action result over the WebSocket, error toast). The proposed unit test feeds each mapper a provider message holding the sentinels 'AKIAQAOAT05SENTINEL1', 'qa-sa@qa-proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com' and 'sk-proj-QAOAT05'.

Then No ConvexError data and no client-visible text contains a sentinel, an access key ID, a service-account email, a project ID or a key.

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): UAT OAT-05 step 1 'no provider API key … anywhere in client-side/browser code' and S01's pattern list ('.iam.gserviceaccount.com' and 'AKIA' are Fails there). A mapper that forwards provider message text able to carry any sentinel to the client is a Fail, quoted with file and line; …

Where it ran: local newspec-c (new Playwright specs); test method CODEREVIEW · Code review; lane planned in the matrix: manual (manual)

S30 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/OAT-05.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Triage (2026-10-14): 1 row.

Issue type: New product issue · environment local · tickets TFA-94423 ready for qa; TFA-94700 ready for qa

When photo reading fails, the server passes the AI provider's raw error line, which can name the Google project or service account, to the physician's browser; OpenAI transcription and the email relay do the same wherever Convex does not hide plain errors.

Evidence: allure d5abcb91-…-result.json; code-review lane. vertex.ts:135/168 copies up to 300 characters of the provider message into ConvexError data.detail. retry.ts:182 and phi.ts:191-196 rethrow it unchanged to the client (scanCensusSheet, scanClinicSchedule, scanPriorNote). openai.ts:19 / transcribe.ts:162 forward OpenAI's error.message (a 401 echoes a masked key), and email.ts:47 forwards the relay error. Clean paths: Bedrock, SES, live session. The S30 oracle says 'No recorded gap or open question applies', and it is not in the dev report. The S05 network capture is the runtime check.
